title: Beliefs and Pillars
lines: This is the largest Islamiat topic in USAT. Questions ask about the articles of faith (iman), the five pillars, and the details of prayer, fasting, zakat and Hajj: meanings of terms, numbers, months and places. Learn the tables below by heart and understand the reason behind each act.
## Articles of faith
| Article | Meaning
| Tawhid | belief in the oneness of Allah, without partner; its opposite, shirk, is the gravest sin
| Angels (malaikah) | created from light; obey Allah and carry out His commands
| Revealed books | Tawrat, Zabur, Injil and the Quran, the final and preserved book
| Prophets (risalah) | sent to every nation; Muhammad (PBUH) is the last (khatm an-nubuwwah)
| The Last Day (akhirah) | resurrection, judgement, Paradise (jannah) and Hell (jahannam)
| Qadar | Allah knows all things and has decreed what will happen; people remain responsible for their choices

The Kalimah Tayyibah declares that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad (PBUH) is His Messenger. Tawhid means that Allah is one in His being and His attributes, that He alone created and sustains everything, and that He alone deserves worship. Surah Al-Ikhlas sums this up.
## Angels and their duties
| Angel | Duty
| Jibreel (AS) | brings revelation to the prophets; called Ruh al-Amin
| Mikail (AS) | in charge of rain and provision
| Israfil (AS) | will blow the trumpet on the Last Day
| Malak al-Mawt | takes souls at death
| Kiraman Katibin | record each person's deeds
| Munkar and Nakir | question the dead in the grave
Life after death passes through Barzakh, the stage between death and resurrection, then the Day of Judgement, when deeds are weighed.
## The five pillars
| Pillar | Key facts
| Shahadah | declaring faith in Allah's oneness and the prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH)
| Salah | five daily prayers, made obligatory on the night of the Mi'raj
| Zakat | 2.5 % of savings above the nisab held for one lunar year; made obligatory in 2 AH
| Sawm | fasting from dawn to sunset in Ramadan; made obligatory in 2 AH
| Hajj | pilgrimage to Makkah in Dhul Hijjah, once in a lifetime for those able
## Salah
| Prayer | Fard rakats
| Fajr | 2
| Zuhr | 4
| Asr | 4
| Maghrib | 3
| Isha | 4
- That makes 17 fard rakats a day. Jumu'ah, 2 rakats with a khutbah, replaces Zuhr on Friday.
- Conditions before prayer include purity (wudu, or ghusl when required), clean clothes and place, facing the qibla (the Kaaba) and the right time.
- If water is not available or harmful, tayammum with clean earth replaces wudu.
- Positions: qiyam (standing), ruku (bowing), sujud (prostration) and qa'dah (sitting). The call to prayer is the adhan; the second call just before the prayer begins is the iqamah.
## Zakat and charity
- Zakat means purification and growth. It is due on savings, gold, silver, trade goods, crops and livestock, at set rates.
- The Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) lists eight groups who may receive zakat, including the poor, the needy, those in debt and travellers in need.
- Sadaqah is voluntary charity; sadaqah jariyah is continuing charity, such as a well or a school. Sadaqat al-Fitr is paid before the Eid al-Fitr prayer.
## Sawm
- The fast runs from dawn (suhur is eaten before it) to sunset (iftar). It teaches taqwa, God-consciousness.
- The sick and travellers may postpone fasts and make them up later. Laylat al-Qadr falls in the last ten nights of Ramadan. Eid al-Fitr is on 1 Shawwal.
## Hajj
| Day of Dhul Hijjah | Rite
| 8th | pilgrims in ihram go to Mina
| 9th | standing at Arafat, the central rite; night at Muzdalifah
| 10th | stoning at Jamarat, sacrifice, shaving or cutting hair, tawaf; Eid al-Adha
| 11th-13th | stoning the three pillars at Mina

- Tawaf is going seven times round the Kaaba; sa'i is walking seven times between Safa and Marwah, recalling Hajar (AS) searching for water. Umrah can be done at any time of year and does not include Arafat.
> How many fard rakats are offered in a day?  (A) 15  (B) 17  (C) 19  (D) 21
> The central rite of Hajj, without which Hajj is not complete, is  (A) tawaf  (B) sa'i  (C) standing at Arafat  (D) sacrifice
> C. The wuquf at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah is the heart of Hajj. The other rites matter, but Arafat is the defining one.
## Traps
! Maghrib, not Fajr, has three fard rakats.
! Eid al-Adha is on 10 Dhul Hijjah, the day after Arafat; Eid al-Fitr is on 1 Shawwal.
! Zakat is 2.5 %, not 10 %. The higher rates you may read about apply to some crops, not savings.
## Quick check
- Six articles of faith; five pillars.
- 17 fard rakats a day; Maghrib has 3.
- Zakat 2.5 % after a lunar year above the nisab.
- Hajj: Mina 8th, Arafat 9th, Eid and Jamarat 10th Dhul Hijjah.
